diagrams.title: From Treasury Record to Recognized Service Fee
diagrams.subtitle: Five operating stages separate client assets from operator earnings.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Use authorized public records and owner-provided evidence. A matching name is only a lead, not proof of entitlement. The canonical first-deal planning window is 3–12 months; filing does not establish a payment date.
diagrams.caption: State-held principal belongs to the owner. Recognize only earned service fees under the applicable accounting policy.

stages.label: Source eligible records
stages.value: Capture the official record and custody dates
stages.detail: Record treasury jurisdiction, property identifier, holder, reported owner, and available dates in SQLite. Preserve source links and follow the portal's access conditions.

stages.label: Resolve ownership
stages.value: Build an evidence-backed owner identity chain
stages.detail: Compare addresses, entity filings, name changes, and signer authority. Escalate mergers, estates, and dissolved entities instead of treating fuzzy matches as ownership.

stages.label: Qualify the engagement
stages.value: Check finder rules before compensated recovery work
stages.detail: Document registration requirements, permitted contracting dates, fee limits, and required agreement terms. Explain the owner's direct-claim option before requesting signature.

stages.label: Submit and track
stages.value: File authorized evidence through the treasury channel
stages.detail: Use the state's accepted claimant or representative process. Log receipt identifiers, evidence requests, response deadlines, and owner-authorized status checks.

stages.label: Reconcile and bill
stages.value: Separate owner proceeds from earned service fees
stages.detail: Prefer treasury payment directly to the owner. Confirm the contractual earning event, invoice the permitted fee, and reconcile fee receivables separately from client principal.

diagrams.title: A Mature Cohort Producing 75 Paid Cases
diagrams.subtitle: Nested case populations support $255,000 in Base-Case service fees.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative mature cohort, not observed conversion performance. Begin with 1,000 distinct owner-property case IDs; each later population is a subset of the preceding population. Assume 75 completed, fee-paid cases recognized within one modeled year at $3,400 average service fees. This is not a 30-day forecast.
diagrams.caption: 1,000 × 40% × 40% × 62.5% × 75% = 75 paid cases; 75 × $3,400 = $255,000 recognized service-fee revenue.

stages.label: Screened prospects
stages.value: 1,000 distinct cases enter the research cohort
stages.detail: Deduplicate by jurisdiction, property identifier, and reported owner. Exclude repeated outreach records rather than inflating the top of the funnel.

stages.label: Evidence-supported matches
stages.value: 400 cases pass preliminary identity and value screening
stages.detail: Forty percent of screened cases have a supportable ownership hypothesis and sufficient expected fees to justify additional research; entitlement remains subject to proof.

stages.label: Lawfully engaged owners
stages.value: 160 matched cases obtain valid service agreements
stages.detail: Forty percent of matched cases proceed after direct-claim disclosure, signer verification, statutory timing checks, and acceptance of a permitted fee structure.

stages.label: Complete claims filed
stages.value: 100 engaged cases reach accepted submission status
stages.detail: Sixty-two and one-half percent of engagements supply the necessary records. Submission acceptance does not mean the treasury has approved ownership or payment.

stages.label: Recovered and fee-paid
stages.value: 75 filed cases produce recognized and collected fees
stages.detail: Seventy-five percent of filed cases complete within the modeled recognition year. Remaining cases stay open, withdraw, or fail; do not book their hoped-for fees.

diagrams.title: Base-Case Revenue to $95,625 Owner Net
diagrams.subtitle: Six bars reconcile $255,000 gross fees to a 37.5% net margin.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Expense categories are an illustrative allocation, not supplied scorecard line items. First and last bars are totals; intermediate negative bars are deductions. Total expenses are $159,375 annually, or $13,281.25 monthly, exceeding the supplied $1,500–$8,000 monthly opex band. That band cannot represent all-in Base expenses; only the modeled $4,000 monthly fixed-overhead component falls inside it.

stages.label: Recognized service fees
stages.value: $255,000 annual operator revenue before modeled expenses
stages.detail: Starting total: 75 paid cases at $3,400 average fees. Exclude treasury disbursements belonging to owners and exclude unearned fees from unresolved claims.

stages.label: Fixed operating overhead
stages.value: Deduct $48,000 for recurring operating infrastructure
stages.detail: Allocate $4,000 monthly to software, insurance, secure document handling, bookkeeping, and administration. Remaining annual contribution after this deduction is $207,000.

stages.label: Contract case delivery
stages.value: Deduct $66,000 for two contractors' delivery work
stages.detail: Budget researcher and claims-administrator capacity at $880 per completed case across 75 cases. Remaining annual contribution after this deduction is $141,000.

stages.label: Research and acquisition
stages.value: Deduct $25,500 for sourcing and owner engagement
stages.detail: Allocate record acquisition, permitted outreach, and unsuccessful prospect research at $340 per completed case. Remaining annual contribution is $115,500.

stages.label: Verification and exceptions
stages.value: Deduct $19,875 for evidence and exception handling
stages.detail: Allocate $265 per completed case to incremental certified records, identity checks, and specialist review. Keep these charges distinct from contractor delivery and fixed overhead.

stages.label: Annual owner net profit
stages.value: $95,625 ending profit equals 37.5% of service fees
stages.detail: Ending total uses the canonical owner-net metric. Conservative remains $60,000 × 25% = $15,000; Scaled remains $450,000 × 50% = $225,000.

diagrams.title: Illustrative Service-Fee Yield by Property Rail
diagrams.subtitle: Compare dollars per completed paid case, not client asset balances.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Selected high-value cases only; these are constructed planning figures, not market averages. Assume 15 paid cases in each of five mutually exclusive property categories. A hypothetical permitted 10% fee connects the example balances to fee yields; actual fee bases, caps, timing, and agreements require state review.
diagrams.caption: 15 × ($5,000 + $4,500 + $3,500 + $2,500 + $1,500) = $255,000 fees on $2,550,000 owner principal at the assumed rate.

stages.label: Corporate government warrants
stages.value: $5,000 service fees per completed paid case
stages.detail: Illustrative $50,000 owner balance at 10%. Confirm that the warrant proceeds are actually state-held, then verify entity continuity and the officer's signing authority.

stages.label: Business vendor checks
stages.value: $4,500 service fees per completed paid case
stages.detail: Illustrative $45,000 owner balance at 10%. Reconcile supplier names, former addresses, and successor entities; exclude government warrants assigned to the preceding category.

stages.label: Insurance proceeds
stages.value: $3,500 service fees per completed paid case
stages.detail: Illustrative $35,000 owner balance at 10%. Resolve policyholder, beneficiary, and estate distinctions before requesting documents or representing a claimant's entitlement.

stages.label: Securities-related cash
stages.value: $2,500 service fees per completed paid case
stages.detail: Illustrative $25,000 recoverable cash balance at 10%. Confirm the state's recorded property form; do not price fees from a speculative current share-market valuation.

stages.label: High-value wage balances
stages.value: $1,500 service fees per completed paid case
stages.detail: Illustrative $15,000 owner balance at 10%. Screen for consolidated high-value balances; ordinary small payroll checks may not support manual recovery economics.

diagrams.title: Four Pre-Flight Checks Before Taking a Case
diagrams.subtitle: Advance only with documented evidence; route failures explicitly.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Read sequentially: passing a check advances to the next check. The numeric field is a check ordinal, not a probability. Determine the applicable jurisdiction and current statutory text for each case; California and New York are concrete examples, not a nationwide substitute.
diagrams.caption: Registration, contract timing, ownership, and secure handling must be resolved before a case enters paid delivery.

stages.label: Finder status and authority
stages.value: Verify required registration and permitted representative activity
stages.detail: Check the treasury's finder requirements and any applicable occupational licensing rules. If required credentials or owner authorization are absent, pause the engagement and identify the specific missing requirement.

stages.label: Agreement timing and fee
stages.value: Test statutory dates, fee limits, and contract terms
stages.detail: For California, examine Code of Civil Procedure section 1582; for New York, Abandoned Property Law section 1416. Document relevant event dates and fee calculations. Route premature cases to a dated revisit list; reject prohibited fees.

stages.label: Ownership and case value
stages.value: Verify the claimant and calculate expected contribution
stages.detail: California Code of Civil Procedure section 1540 anchors the claim process. Escalate conflicting identities or successor rights. Decline cases whose expected lawful fees cannot cover research, evidence, delivery, and collection costs.

stages.label: Privacy and owner understanding
stages.value: Protect identity evidence and disclose direct claiming
stages.detail: Assess California Civil Code section 1798.81.5 where applicable. Use restricted encrypted storage, multifactor authentication, and expiring document links. Explain that the owner can claim directly; pause if understanding or secure evidence collection remains unresolved.

diagrams.title: Three Core Seats, Two Scale Seats
diagrams.subtitle: Keep accountable ownership explicit as annual service fees grow.
diagrams.assumptions_note: FT means full-time; C means contractor. Conservative and Base use one FT plus two C, totaling three people. Scaled uses two FT plus three C, totaling five people. Each numeric value is one person; the final two seats belong only to the scaled pod.
diagrams.caption: Core pod: $60,000 revenue / $15,000 net or $255,000 / $95,625. Scaled five-person pod: $450,000 revenue / $225,000 net.

stages.label: Founder and accountable operator
stages.value: Core seat: one full-time operating owner
stages.detail: Own engagement decisions, treasury relationships, fee pricing, dispute resolution, and cash reconciliation. Review exception queues rather than delegating final ownership judgments to an automated matcher.

stages.label: Records investigator
stages.value: Core seat: one contractor researching owner evidence
stages.detail: Maintain source provenance, entity histories, address matches, and duplicate controls. Access only assigned case records; return ambiguous matches with explicit evidence gaps instead of confident guesses.

stages.label: Claims administrator
stages.value: Core seat: one contractor managing submission completeness
stages.detail: Prepare authorized claim packets, track treasury receipts, request missing evidence, and maintain aging reports. Never convert a status update into an unsupported promise about payment timing.

stages.label: Delivery and queue manager
stages.value: Scale addition: one full-time case operations lead
stages.detail: Coordinate researcher capacity, evidence response times, handoffs, and receivable follow-up. Add this seat when measured backlog and collected-fee economics support ongoing payroll, not merely a larger prospect list.

stages.label: Complex-case specialist
stages.value: Scale addition: one contractor reviewing exceptional cases
stages.detail: Handle documented entity succession, estate evidence, or jurisdiction-specific specialist work within their credentials. Escalate matters requiring licensed counsel instead of expanding administrative staff authority.

diagrams.title: Allocate Startup Capital Before Scaling Outreach
diagrams.subtitle: Four buckets total $20,000 within the $5,000–$35,000 range.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values describe one $20,000 startup allocation. Details also provide lean and expanded allocations totaling $5,000 and $35,000 respectively. These are deployment budgets, not projected revenue or sufficient runway for every case. Owner living costs are outside these allocations.
diagrams.caption: Central allocation: $4,000 + $6,000 + $5,000 + $5,000 = $20,000. A 3–12 month first-deal window requires separate runway planning against actual recurring and variable costs.

stages.label: Jurisdiction and agreement setup
stages.value: $4,000 central allocation for lawful engagement setup
stages.detail: Lean allocation $1,000; expanded allocation $7,000. Fund applicable registration, jurisdiction-specific agreement drafting, and focused professional review before purchasing a large prospect inventory.

stages.label: Secure records and workflow
stages.value: $6,000 central allocation for evidence-handling infrastructure
stages.detail: Lean allocation $1,500; expanded allocation $10,000. Configure Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace access controls, encrypted endpoints, backup restoration tests, and a minimal claim-status database.

stages.label: Research and owner acquisition
stages.value: $5,000 central allocation for measured prospect development
stages.detail: Lean allocation $1,000; expanded allocation $8,000. Purchase authorized records, obtain certified entity documents, and test transparent outreach. Track spend per evidence-supported case before increasing volume.

stages.label: Operating liquidity reserve
stages.value: $5,000 central allocation for early cash timing gaps
stages.detail: Lean allocation $1,500; expanded allocation $10,000. At $4,000 monthly fixed overhead, the central reserve covers only 1.25 months before variable costs; arrange additional runway or reduce the initial cost structure.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to a Controlled Recovery Operation
diagrams.subtitle: Build a qualified pipeline without promising a treasury payout.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Four weekly milestones establish operating readiness, not first-deal completion. The canonical first-deal window remains 3–12 months. Pilot counts are workload targets rather than predicted engagement or collection results.
diagrams.caption: Finish the month with traceable records, reviewed agreements, secure evidence handling, and an owner-authorized claim queue.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.value: Select one jurisdiction and document the operating rules
stages.detail: Choose a treasury and two property categories. Capture finder requirements, statutory event dates, fee limits, claim evidence requirements, and direct-claim instructions. Budget fixed overhead and document the funding gap.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.value: Configure secure intake and review twenty-five records
stages.detail: Create a SQLite case register with stable identifiers, source links, access owners, and next-action dates. Test restricted uploads and backups. Manually review 25 public records to calibrate duplicate and identity rules.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.value: Test transparent outreach against ten screened prospects
stages.detail: Where permitted, contact ten evidence-supported prospects without implying government affiliation. Explain direct claiming, document responses, and execute only agreements whose timing, fees, and signer authority have been checked.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.value: Prepare eligible packets and inspect the evidence backlog
stages.detail: Submit only complete, authorized claims; otherwise log the exact missing evidence and responsible person. Review case aging, estimated contribution, and cash runway. Schedule weekly treasury-status and receivable reviews.
